sovereign_country.strategic_role: 全球海事商船注册旗国、借鉴特拉华州公司法的非公开发行实体

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Commercial Shipbuilding of Deep-Sea Dry Cargo and Container Vessels

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Republic of the Marshall Islands (unitary national jurisdiction; single corporate registry administered by the Office of the Registrar of Corporations)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid (Common Law foundation; corporate and maritime statutes modeled on U.S. Delaware law and the Marshall Islands Maritime Act 1990; 1979 Constitution as supreme law; residual customary law)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Compact of Free Association between the United States and the Republic of the Marshall Islands (1986; Amended Compact 2003) – investment, trade and economic provisions
PACER-Plus (Pacific Agreement on Closer Economic Relations Plus, signed 2017) – regional trade and investment facilitation
Tax Information Exchange Agreements with Australia and New Zealand (no comprehensive double taxation agreement in force)
U.S.-RMI Treaty on Fisheries (1987) – contextual maritime economic agreement

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Anti-Money Laundering and Countering the Financing of Terrorism Act 2018 (as amended), FIU AML/CFT Regulations and Guidelines; Banking Act 1992 (as amended); International Banking Act 2002 (as amended); Business Corporations Act 1990 (as amended) – registered agent record-keeping and beneficial ownership duties; U.N. Security Council sanctions implementing regulations.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of approved Articles of Incorporation (charter)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Office of the Registrar of Corporations (Ministry of Finance; administered by International Registries, Inc.)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille – Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade, Majuro

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Certificate of Existence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Office of the Registrar of Corporations (Ministry of Finance)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille – Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade, Majuro

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incumbency (directors, officers, registered agent) and Register of Directors
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed registered agent / International Registries, Inc.
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization in country of execution followed by Hague Apostille

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Registered Agent Consent form and Registered Office attestation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization followed by Hague Apostille (Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory risk-based PEP identification (individuals, family members, and close associates), screening of all UBOs and signatories against OFAC SDN/Consolidated Sanctions List, U.N. Security Council sanctions (1267/1988, 1718, 2231, and country-specific resolutions), EU consolidated sanctions list, and RMI domestic restricted-persons advisories; enhanced due diligence, senior-management approval, source-of-wealth verification, and ongoing transaction monitoring are required for PEP and high-risk shipbuilding counterparties under the 2018 AML/CFT Act.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Marshall Islands Corporate Registry – Office of the Registrar of Corporations (Ministry of Finance), delegated administrator: International Registries, Inc. (IRI); online filing via IRI's corporate registry portal (www.register-iri.com)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: English is the official statutory language; corporate names must be rendered in the Latin/Roman alphabet and include a corporate designator (Corporation, Incorporated, Company, Limited, or an abbreviation) per the name provisions of the Business Corporations Act 1990; non-Latin script names are accepted only with a notarized transliteration and certified translation.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Bank, Banking, Trust, Trustee, Insurance, Assurance, Reinsurance, Fiduciary, Finance (where implying regulated financial services) – require prior financial license or Ministry of Finance consent
Chamber of Commerce, University, College, Red Cross, Cooperative, Guild – require prior approval or are prohibited absent statutory entitlement
Government, Republic of the Marshall Islands, Official, State, National – prohibited absent express written consent of the Ministry of Finance
Marshall Islands (as a standalone element implying state connection) – subject to objection by the Registrar
Any name causing confusion with an existing registered domestic or foreign entity, or otherwise contrary to public policy
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A cleared name is reserved for 30 days from the date of clearance; extension is available in successive 30-day increments upon written application through a licensed registered agent and payment of the renewal tariff before expiry. On rejection, the applicant may resubmit up to two alternative names; a written administrative appeal with supporting evidence may be lodged with the Registrar of Corporations within 14 days of the rejection notice; where rejection is based on similarity, a notarized letter of consent from the prior rights holder may cure the objection. The Registrar's final decision may be appealed to the High Court of the Marshall Islands under the Business Corporations Act 1990.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual/serviced office is acceptable solely for the statutory registered office and registered agent address under the Business Corporations Act 1990; it cannot satisfy the commercial substance requirements of an operating shipyard (ISIC 3011). Physical industrial premises, a valid land lease or ownership title, EPA environmental clearance, and a locally engaged operational manager are mandatory for the business license.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High – approximately 70-80% likelihood of unannounced physical inspection within the first 12 months of operations, driven by RMI Environmental Protection Authority site inspections, customs and border controls at shipyard facilities, social security and labor compliance checks, and Ministry of Finance business license verification.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Name clearance and preliminary search (up to three proposed names)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Office of the Registrar of Corporations via IRI
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory registry tariff (IRI published fee schedule)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Filing fee – Articles of Incorporation (Business Corporation)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Ministry of Finance – Office of the Registrar of Corporations
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory government fee schedule under the Business Corporations Act 1990

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered agent and registered office service (first annual term)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: IRI-approved Marshall Islands corporate services provider
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for non-resident business corporations

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: AML/CFT onboarding and CDD/EDD file setup, UBO identification, PEP and OFAC/UN sanctions screening
Notarization of UBO, director, and signatory records (four vouchers)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade, Majuro

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Business license application – first year (industrial shipbuilding / manufacturing)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Ministry of Finance – Division of Revenue
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Business License Act 1990 annual tariff for industrial category

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Environmental pre-clearance and shipyard siting application
Pre-incorporation legal due diligence and UBO piercing opinion (structured per OFAC/PEP matrix)
Maritime installment LC and escrow structure legal memorandum (pre-banking package)

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act (BCA), Marshall Islands Revised Code Title 24 (Associations), Chapter 1; formation provisions at Sections 24.201–24.206, 24.210–24.213, and 24.601–24.603 (registered office and registered agent).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Office of the Registrar of Corporations, Marshall Islands Corporate Registry, Majuro, Republic of the Marshall Islands; filings are made through a licensed resident registered agent.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation, together with registered agent consent and the BCA prescribed cover/transmittal sheet.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital is imposed by the Business Corporations Act; shares may be issued with par value or no par value, and no escrow deposit or paid-in capital remittance is required before incorporation or shipyard license application.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: The Board consents to and ratifies all subscription agreements of the initial shareholders. The share register shall reflect each subscriber’s shares as set forth in the subscription schedule. The registered office of the Corporation shall be the address of its registered agent in Majuro, Republic of the Marshall Islands, as stated in the Articles of Incorporation. The following members of the board are appointed as officers of the Corporation: President, Secretary, and Treasurer. Each officer shall serve at the pleasure of the Board and may receive compensation as subsequently determined. The President and Secretary are jointly and severally authorized to execute and deliver certificates, banking forms, statutory filings, and the shipyard operating license applications necessary to commence business.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate name reservation and appointment of registered agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Office of the Registrar of Corporations, Marshall Islands Corporate Registry, through a licensed resident registered agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name reservation request with the first and alternative corporate names, together with the registered agent’s signed consent to act. Confirm that the proposed name is distinguishable from existing Marshall Islands entities and is acceptable under BCA suffix requirements.
required_dossiers: Registered agent consent and acceptance letter
Authorized applicant identification or KYC documentation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected for confusing similarity, select the approved alternative name and re-file the reservation; a new reservation can be filed without loss of the original filing fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and execution of constitutional and governance documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Company counsel and registered agent, coordinated with the Office of the Registrar of Corporations
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the Articles of Incorporation and Bylaws, including authorised share structure, corporate purpose covering commercial shipbuilding and repair of deep-sea container vessels, registered office address, registered agent, and first directors. Execute the documents by the incorporator and initial directors as required.
required_dossiers: Subscriber subscription schedule and share ledger
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar raises a deficiency in the corporate purpose or legal formalities, amend the draft and resubmit; execution pages may be re-signed by the same incorporator without affecting the original completion date.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Statutory filing and payment of incorporation fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Office of the Registrar of Corporations, Marshall Islands Corporate Registry, via electronic submission through the registered agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the signed Articles of Incorporation, registered agent consent, and payment of the $250 official filing fee. Request standard or expedited review; upon approval the Registrar endorses the articles and issues the Certificate of Incorporation.
required_dossiers: Government fee remittance or treasury receipt
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried, file a Notice of Correction through the registered agent within 30 days, cure the stated defect, and pay any administrative correction fee; if the deadline is missed, the application is discontinued and a new filing may be required.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First organizational meeting and initial corporate acts
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: First directors and corporate secretary, with support of the registered agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the first board meeting or execute a unanimous written consent adopting the Bylaws, ratifying share subscriptions, confirming the registered office, and appointing the initial officers. Issue share certificates and record ownership in the share ledger.
required_dossiers: Unanimous written consent or minutes of the first board meeting
Share subscription list and share certificates
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If an omission in the organizational acts is discovered, adopt a curative unanimous written consent effective retroactively, provided no rights of third parties are prejudiced and the Registrar’s records remain unaffected.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Certificate collection and commencement of licensing preparation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Office of the Registrar of Corporations and corporate registered agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Collect the Certificate of Incorporation and certified copies from the Registrar; verify that the registered agent, office, directors, and officers are correctly recorded. Prepare the corporate good standing certificate request and coordinate evidence of entity existence for the shipyard operating license and bank account opening.
required_dossiers: Request for certificate of good standing
Registered office and registered agent confirmation record
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If any certificate contains a name, date, or registered office discrepancy, apply to the Registrar for a certificate of correction with supporting articles; correction is generally issued within two business days.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Industrial Licensing Board, Ministry of Resources and Development, Republic of the Marshall Islands, with technical review by the Maritime and Ports Authority
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Commercial Shipyard Facility Operating License for Shipbuilding and Vessel Repair (ISIC 3011)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environmental Protection Authority of the Republic of the Marshall Islands
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category A – Full Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) mandatory for new coastal shipyard construction, including slipways, dry dock, quayside facilities, and marine discharge infrastructure.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Applicable RMIEPA permit conditions require treated industrial wastewater effluent within limits of pH 6–9, biochemical oxygen demand (BOD5) ≤ 30 mg/L, total suspended solids ≤ 50 mg/L, and oil and grease ≤ 10 mg/L; VOC emissions from paint, abrasive blasting, and welding must be captured through engineered ventilation and reported; hazardous wastes must be segregated, stored, and removed in compliance with RMIEPA hazardous waste regulations and MARPOL Annex V requirements.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety clearance certificate from the relevant local fire authority; civil defense structural load inspection covering fabrication halls, cranes, dry dock gates, slipways, and fuel or solvent storage; occupational health and workplace clearance under the Marshall Islands workplace safety rules, including approval of confined-space entry, hot work, crane operations, and emergency evacuation plans.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Marshall Islands Revenue and Customs Administration (RICA), an executive agency under the Ministry of Finance, Delap, Majuro Atoll; registry functions are divided between the Registrar of Corporations (Business Corporations Act 1990) and the Marshall Islands Maritime Administrator (Maritime Act 1990); taxpayer registration and customs filing are administered through the RICA official portal and the licensed registered-agent network.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A non-resident Business Corporation (MH_BC) procures its statutory tax identity as follows: (1) incorporation under the Business Corporations Act through a government-licensed Registered Agent, generating the corporate registration number and Certificate of Incorporation; (2) submission of a Taxpayer Registration Application (Form TR-1) to RICA, attaching the Certificate of Incorporation, registered agent consent, director particulars, and a declaration of non-resident status; (3) issuance of a Marshall Islands Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN) ordinarily within 3–5 business days; (4) where the entity has any in-country economic footprint, supplementary registration for Gross Revenue Tax and a Customs Importer/Exporter Code is required; (5) for the offshore shipbuilding model, the entity files a Non-Resident Domestic Corporation (NRDC) status declaration with the Registrar to confirm the absence of Marshall Islands-source revenue and to secure exemption from income tax and gross revenue tax. No minimum capital, local director, or physical office is required.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: The Marshall Islands has no check-the-box or hybrid-mismatch classification regime; however, the following statutory elections apply to the MH_BC: (i) Non-Resident Domestic Corporation (NRDC) election under the Business Corporations Act, rendering the entity exempt from income tax and Gross Revenue Tax on all foreign-source earnings and exports; (ii) International Ship Registry election under the Marshall Islands Maritime Act, which confirms income-tax exemption for vessel ownership, charter, and shipbuilding-related revenues where the vessel is titled through the Marshall Islands International Ship Registry; (iii) Gross Revenue Tax de minimis election for entities with gross revenue below the statutory registration threshold; and (iv) foreign-source income designation election for ISIC 3011 shipbuilding contract proceeds, placing the delivery and title-transfer transactions outside the Republic's territorial sourcing rules. No partnership or disregarded-entity elections exist under the Income Tax Act 1989.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: No national VAT or GST; indirect taxation comprises a 3% Gross Revenue Tax (GRT) on businesses earning revenue sourced within the Republic, customs import duties under the Customs Ordinance 1991, and selective excise duties on petroleum, tobacco, and alcohol; exports of newly built deep-sea dry cargo and container vessels are entirely outside the indirect tax net.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: GRT registration: USD 5,000 annual gross revenue threshold for businesses with in-country revenue; a fully non-resident MH_BC deriving no Marshall Islands-source revenue is not registrable for GRT; customs registration: a Customs Importer/Exporter Code is mandatory for any physical movement of goods across the Republic's border, irrespective of value; no VAT threshold applies because no VAT law exists.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No electronic invoicing, real-time fiscal clearance, API-integrated clearance, or digital stamping mandate exists under Marshall Islands law. RICA operates a hybrid paper-digital customs environment; export declarations may be lodged electronically through approved customs brokers, but continuous transaction controls, national e-invoicing frameworks, and fiscal data reporting to tax authorities are not statutory requirements.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Statutory VAT zero-rating is inapplicable because the Republic levies no VAT or GST. Export substantive relief is instead achieved through the territorial sourcing rules of the Income Tax Act 1989: revenue from the export sale of an ocean container vessel is sourced at the place where the contract is made and title passes; where delivery occurs at a foreign shipyard or on international waters, the profit is non-sourced and therefore exempt from Marshall Islands income tax and GRT. The exemption is further secured by the NRDC election and, where the vessel is flagged under the Marshall Islands International Ship Registry, by the Maritime Act exemptions for shipbuilding, repair, and sale; no export tax or export duty is levied.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Form C-IX) for the vessel or its components when physically leaving Marshall Islands jurisdiction
Bill of Lading or Sea Waybill evidencing ocean transport and delivery to the non-resident buyer
Commercial Invoice and executed shipbuilding contract (ISIC 3011) detailing price, delivery terms, and title-transfer point
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank credit advice evidencing USD receipt of the export sale proceeds from the foreign buyer
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: RICA may open assessments within six years of the relevant tax period and, where an export exemption or NRDC status is found to have been misapplied, recover the full amount of unpaid tax with a 10% monthly delinquency surcharge capped at 50%, plus interest at the statutory rate (prime rate plus 2%). Willful false declaration in support of export exemption constitutes a criminal offense under the Income Tax Act 1989, punishable by a fine of up to USD 10,000 and imprisonment of up to three years per count; false customs export declarations attract forfeiture of goods and civil penalties up to 40% of declared value under the Customs Ordinance. The Anti-Money Laundering Act 2018 imposes record-keeping and transaction-reporting obligations on shipyard export transactions, with corporate fines up to USD 500,000 for failures connected with export proceeds; RICA may additionally revoke the NRDC exemption certificate upon a finding that management and control were in fact exercised in the Marshall Islands, triggering retrospective clawback of all exempted profit from the inception of the exemption period.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Office of the Financial Institutions Commissioner (FIC), Republic of the Marshall Islands
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Republic of the Marshall Islands (RMI) adopts the United States Dollar (USD) as its official legal tender and maintains a completely liberalized capital account with zero exchange controls. There are no statutory barriers to capital account convertibility, no licensing requirements for foreign direct investment, and no restrictions on the repatriation of dividends, loan repayments, or liquidation proceeds for non-resident shareholders. Profit remittance is subject only to standard corporate solvency tests, board authorization, and ordinary AML/KYC screening. The absence of a domestic central bank and the use of USD eliminate any convertibility delay or multiple-currency risk within the jurisdiction.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: RMI maintains no export proceeds surrender obligation. A shipyard entity is not required to convert export or construction milestone receipts into local currency because USD is the domestic currency. All export proceeds may be retained in USD, held in offshore correspondent accounts, used directly for foreign currency disbursements, or repatriated without a mandatory conversion timeline or a prescribed liquidation period.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: National Bank of the Marshall Islands (NBMI)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Offshore digital Electronic Money Institutions (EMIs) have severely constrained viability in the RMI banking ecosystem. The domestic regulatory framework does not provide for non-resident EMI licensing, and all RMI-chartered banks require a licensed resident presence or a registered foreign entity with a valid RMI business license. Unlicensed offshore payment processors cannot be used as primary treasury clearing rails due to domestic banking prohibitions on passing funds through unregulated intermediaries. An RMI shipyard is therefore required to maintain its primary operating and escrow accounts within a locally chartered, federally insured or correspondent-linked domestic bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Directors of a non-resident shipyard entity are generally required to complete one physical KYC interview at the bank's Majuro branch before the account is fully activated. A limited remote pre-screening via video conference and digital document upload may be accepted for preliminary account approval, but the final risk assessment sign-off for the Medium-Risk Enhanced maritime manufacturing classification mandates an in-person board resolution and certified corporate document inspection.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sector-based Enhanced Due Diligence (EDD) for ISIC 3011 commercial shipbuilding and multi-million-dollar maritime installment payments.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Execute copy of the commercial shipbuilding contract, vessel construction schedule and milestone payment terms, RMI Business License, certified Articles of Incorporation and Bylaws, original Board Resolution authorizing account opening and treasury operations, and a detailed project cash-flow waterfall covering installments, supplier disbursements, and contingency reserves.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opacity in the non-resident Ultimate Beneficial Ownership (UBO) structure or high-risk passport jurisdictions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Formal UBO declaration per RMI AML/CFT framework, certified passport copies and proof of address for every natural person holding a direct or indirect interest of 10% or more, source-of-wealth statements for shareholders, bank references from prior financial institutions, and a formal legal opinion issued by RMI-licensed counsel confirming the validity of the ownership cascade and the absence of shell nominee arrangements.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: All inward capital injections and construction milestone payments must be routed via SWIFT MT103 or MT202 from the payee's verified corporate bank account. The remittance must carry an accurate purpose code consistent with the underlying commercial transaction, such as Subscription, Trade Payment, or Construction Disbursement. Before crediting the account, the receiving bank will require a Beneficiary Account Certification, a Board Resolution, and a Source of Funds (SOF) declaration. For each vessel milestone, the inbound wire advice must be matched to the corresponding invoice and, where applicable, an independent classification-society progress certificate to satisfy all statutory and internal AML scanning protocols.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound settlement to foreign equipment suppliers, subcontractors, and technical agents must be executed via SWIFT MT103 direct transfers or MT202 corporate-to-corporate transfers. For large-ticket items and international equipment procurement, the preferred clearing rail is an irrevocable commercial Letter of Credit (LC), advised and, when possible, confirmed through a major U.S. money-center bank with established correspondent banking relationships to RMI. Each disbursement must align strictly with the approved invoice, the vessel construction budget, and the signed treasury mandate; no cash payments or third-party offset arrangements are permissible.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: USD/foreign-currency forwards executed with a licensed cross-border banking counterparty to fix the USD cost of imported equipment and subcontractor services
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) used only where a non-convertible currency exposure exists in a supplier jurisdiction and economic substance can be demonstrated
Cross-currency interest rate swaps (CCIRS) for aligning a project finance liability or a trade finance facility in a non-USD currency to the USD functional currency of the shipyard

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Report (Business Corporations Act, Section 104) — base government fee USD 200 for authorized capital up to USD 50,000; higher graduated tiers apply above that threshold
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of Corporations, Republic of the Marshall Islands (filed through the licensed Registered Agent; registry administration outsourced to the Association of Registered Agents)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due within 30 days after each anniversary of incorporation (anniversary-based, not calendar-year); the report reconfirms registered office, registered agent, directors, officers, and share capital as of the anniversary date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of USD 200 where the report is received after the 30-day grace window; failure to file and pay for two consecutive years exposes the corporation to involuntary dissolution and administrative strike-off by the Registrar; reinstatement requires settlement of all arrearages, accrued penalties, and reinstatement fees.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Business License Renewal and Gross Receipts Return (Business Licenses Act 1990) — applicable only if the shipyard carries on taxable activity, operates premises, or employs staff in the Marshall Islands; not applicable to a non-resident exempt Business Corporation with no RMI-source operations
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Revenue and Taxation Division, Ministry of Finance, Republic of the Marshall Islands (Business License Office)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on or before 28 February covering the prior calendar year; a newly commenced business must obtain a license before shipyard operations begin
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Business license tax of 3% of annual gross receipts applies where taxable operations exist; late payment attracts a 10% penalty and suspension of the license, which prohibits further lawful business operations in the Marshall Islands until renewal and all penalties are paid.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial Ownership Confirmation — confidential beneficial ownership schedule lodged concurrently with the Annual Report and updated upon any share transfer or ownership change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of Corporations (lodged via the licensed Registered Agent); disclosed only to the Marshall Islands Financial Intelligence Unit and competent law-enforcement authorities
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filed with the Annual Report at the incorporation anniversary (within 30 days); any share transfer or change in beneficial ownership must be recorded and submitted within 21 days of the event
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to maintain or update beneficial ownership records, or submission of false beneficial ownership information, is an offence under the Business Corporations Act (as amended) and the RMI Anti-Money-Laundering Regulations; the corporation and its registered agent may be fined and the agent's license may be suspended.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No mandatory statutory audit applies to any Marshall Islands business corporation; the Business Corporations Act imposes no revenue, asset, or shareholder audit trigger. An independent audit arises only as a contractual condition imposed by lenders, escrow banks, buyers, export-credit agencies, or classification societies within the shipyard financing and vessel-sale transaction chain.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: No prescribed statutory accounting standard; the BCA requires books and records that fairly reflect the corporation's financial position. IFRS or US GAAP is the accepted market standard for shipyard operations and ship-financing documentation. Non-resident exempt Business Corporations are not subject to RMI income tax and file no national corporate income tax return.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: At each annual report date the directors must re-confirm the beneficial ownership schedule held by the registered agent; every share transfer is recorded in the Register of Members and the confidential beneficial ownership schedule is updated within 21 days; the schedule is not publicly searchable and is produced only to the Financial Intelligence Unit or a competent court upon lawful request.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (issued shares, classes, transfers, redemption, and forfeiture records)
Minute Book (shareholder and board meeting minutes and unanimous written consents)
Accounting records under Section 53 of the Business Corporations Act
Confidential Beneficial Ownership Register (maintained at the registered agent's office)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 15,000 – 35,000 per annum (only where a lender, escrow bank, or ship-purchase agreement mandates a certified audit)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 3% flat corporate income tax on net income derived from sources within the Republic (Income Tax Act 1989, as amended); the same 3% rate is the headline Gross Revenue Tax on gross revenue from business carried on in the Republic, with GRT creditable against the net income tax.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Effective 0% for a Non-Resident Business Corporation (MH_BC) that derives no Marshall Islands-source income: RMI taxation is territorial, foreign-source shipbuilding income is exempt, there is no capital gains tax, no VAT/GST, no minimum corporate tax, and no branch remittance tax. A 3% GRT applies only to gross revenue actually earned inside the Republic, and GRT paid is a credit against the 3% net income tax.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: RMI Corporate Income Tax Return (statutory schedule under the Income Tax Act 1989, commonly referenced as Form RMI-C-1120), filed electronically through the RMI Tax & Revenue Division e-filing portal; a Non-Resident Business Corporation with no RMI-source income obtains a 'No Return Required' status and files a nil declaration only where the shipyard business licence so demands.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual, based on the fiscal year-end; quarterly provisional instalments and quarterly GRT returns are required for any taxpayer deriving RMI-source gross revenue, with instalments due 45 days after the end of each calendar quarter.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual return is due on or before the last day of the fourth month following the close of the taxable year (30 April for a calendar-year taxpayer); the Tax & Revenue Division may grant an extension of up to six months upon written application. For non-resident corporations with no RMI-source activity, no filing deadline is triggered.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross revenue and trade receipts for the taxable period, before deductions, from all sources, with a jurisdictional attachment for RMI-sourced and foreign-sourced income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter only revenue attributable to Marshall Islands sources; revenue from international shipbuilding contracts for ocean container vessels is foreign-source and must be excluded. Leave zero if the shipyard operates wholly outside the Republic.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 2 — Cost of Goods Sold and Deductible Expenses
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Direct materials (steel, engines), outsourced fabrication labour, dry-dock costs, depreciation of shipyard tooling, administrative overheads, and licensed fees attributable to the reported revenue.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Allocate costs on the same RMI-source apportionment basis used in Box 1; intercompany charges from affiliates must be supported by contemporaneous arm's length documentation; a qualifying non-resident shipyard with no RMI-source income may enter zero.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net income computed as Box 1 less Box 2, before the statutory credit.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If all shipyard income is foreign-source, enter zero. A non-resident corporation must not include worldwide income from vessel construction performed outside the Republic.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross corporate income tax computed by applying the 3% flat rate to Box 3.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Leave zero unless RMI-source net income is present; the 3% rate is the ceiling for non-resident corporations.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Credit for GRT already paid on the same proceeds during the year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim only GRT actually remitted to the RMI Tax & Revenue Division on RMI-source shipyard revenue; no credit is available for foreign taxes paid.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 6 — Tax Due / Refund and Authorised Signatory
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net tax payable or refundable, declaration of accuracy, and signature of the authorised director or resident agent.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident director or the licensed registered agent must sign; a knowingly false nil return is a criminal omission and converts the filing into a fraud claim.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: 5% per month or part of a month, capped at 25% of the tax shown due; late payment: statutory interest at the prevailing rate compounded monthly; failure to file after official notice is a misdemeanour carrying a fine of up to US$5,000 and/or one year of imprisonment; a wilfully false or fraudulent return is a felony punishable by a fine up to double the tax evaded and/or five years of imprisonment.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0%. The Republic of the Marshall Islands imposes no withholding tax on dividends distributed by a Business Corporation to non-resident shareholders, whether paid from shipyard operating profits, liquidation proceeds, or investment income; no such WHT exists in the Income Tax Act or the GRT Act.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The RMI maintains no comprehensive double taxation agreement network. The only operative bilateral instruments are the US-RMI Tax Information Exchange Agreement and the US FATCA Model 1 Intergovernmental Agreement. Consequently there is no DTA withholding rate to invoke for dividends, interest, or royalties. To the extent a shareholder's home jurisdiction grants a foreign tax credit, the RMI Tax & Revenue Division will issue a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) upon written application supported by the certificate of incorporation, board resolution, registered agent confirmation, and a statement of the 0% rate applied; the TRC is the sole administrative device used to evidence RMI tax status abroad.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory withholding on interest and royalties paid to non-residents: 0%. No DTA treaty rate is available because no comprehensive double taxation agreement is in force; foreign lenders and IP licensors receive payments free of RMI withholding, although a non-resident recipient deriving royalties for IP used in a shipyard physically located in the Republic remains self-assessable on any RMI-source income.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Not applicable — the Marshall Islands has not adopted OECD Chapter V Local File or Master File rules, and no monetary threshold in Marshall Islands law triggers a mandatory transfer pricing filing. The arm's length principle is, however, embedded in the anti-avoidance provisions of the Income Tax Act and will be applied where RMI-source profits are assessed; for a medium-risk enhanced shipyard BC, contemporaneous pricing records for every cross-border intercompany transaction are recommended, with a practical internal benchmark of a USD 500,000 gross-receipts threshold for preparing a full local transfer pricing file.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: The Marshall Islands Economic Substance Act, embedded in the Business Corporations Act framework, applies to 'relevant activities' comprising banking, insurance, shipping operations, pure IP holding, and financing/leasing. Commercial shipbuilding (ISIC 3011) is a manufacturing activity and is not a designated relevant activity; however, if the same Business Corporation charters, operates, or bareboat-leases the container vessels it builds, the 'shipping operations' category is triggered, demanding (i) management and control exercised in the RMI, (ii) adequate local premises and qualified employees, and (iii) annually documented core income-generating activity. Shipyard BCs should nonetheless maintain a substance file — board minutes, local agent attendance, employer registrations, and physical yard records — to preserve the non-resident tax-exempt status and avoid recharacterisation as a tax-resident shell.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Claiming non-resident tax-exempt status while the shipyard's directors actually manage and control the business from the Republic, or knowingly filing a zero return while revenue is derived from building or repairing vessels inside Marshall Islands territory, or artificially diverting RMI-source design and fabrication fees to a foreign affiliate.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Civil fraud penalty of up to 75% of the understated tax plus interest from the due date; criminal evasion is a felony under the Income Tax Act carrying a fine up to double the tax evaded and imprisonment up to five years; the vessel under construction is additionally subject to forfeiture proceedings under the Maritime Act.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign false returns are personally and severally liable for the corporate tax and penalties where the company is a mere instrumentality; the RMI High Court may issue asset-preservation and travel-restraint orders, and individual directors face criminal indictment, travel bans, surrender of passports, and imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining the Business Corporation and shipyard licence as a letterbox operation with no physical yard, no production employees, no board records, and no locally verifiable management; using passive intercompany invoicing to strip revenue out of a shipyard that is in fact operated from the Republic; chartering vessels without any RMI management and control.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Revocation of the Business Corporation registration and the mandatory ISIC 3011 shipyard licence; reclassification of the entity as RMI tax-resident with retroactive assessment of the 3% income tax plus a late-payment surcharge; public naming by the Registrar of Corporations and exclusion from the RMI Maritime Registry.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Executive and nominee directors are jointly and severally liable for the unpaid tax and penalties where the corporation is a facade; the High Court may prohibit directors from leaving the Republic, disqualify them from serving on any RMI-registered entity, and appoint a receiver over their personal assets.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML/CFT Violation — Suspicious Payments and Missing STR
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Receiving maritime instalment payments under Letters of Credit or escrow drawdowns from sanctioned, shell, or politically exposed counterparties; structuring cash receipts to avoid internal reporting thresholds; failing to file Suspicious Transaction Reports with the RMI Financial Intelligence Unit; running a shipyard at 'Medium_Risk_Enhanced' tier without an approved AML/CFT compliance programme.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Monetary penalty of up to US$250,000 per violation under the AML/CFT legislation, asset-freezing and confiscation orders over contract proceeds, revocation of the statutory shipyard licence, and referral to the Asia/Pacific Group on Money Laundering and the Egmont Group for transnational enforcement.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, compliance officers, and beneficial owners face personal criminal prosecution for money laundering, removal from the RMI company register, blacklisting by the FIU, High Court travel bans, and surrender of passports pending investigation; fraudulent concealment of beneficial ownership additionally attracts personal fines and imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Constructing or outfitting ocean container vessels without the statutorily required shipyard business licence; using a dormant non-resident Business Corporation to front for an unlicensed yard physically operating on Marshall Islands territory; continuing work after licence suspension.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fine of up to US$50,000 per unlicensed vessel constructed, forfeiture of any ship built or repaired without licence, and a continuing penalty of US$1,000 per day of unlicensed operation; the licence authority may also strike the entity from the corporate register.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are personally liable for the unpaid licence fees, penalties, and costs of forfeiture; a criminal conviction leads to disqualification from holding directorships in the RMI, personal monetary judgments, and imprisonment for continued operation after revocation.
